subtopic: CUDA / Register spill and local memory
learningObjective: Understand what CUDA 'local memory' actually is and when register spilling occurs.
stem: In CUDA, when nvcc reports register spilling to 'local memory', which statement is correct?

options.text: 'Local memory' in CUDA is per-thread private storage that lives in global memory (backed by L1 / L2 / DRAM), not on-chip; spilled registers therefore incur high-latency accesses through the memory hierarchy, and heavy spilling typically kills performance.
'Local memory' is a small dedicated on-chip cache (~4 KB per thread) that is faster than shared memory; register spills into it are essentially free and do not affect kernel throughput.
'Local memory' is the same physical memory as shared memory; the compiler decides at build time which lanes get 'local' vs 'shared' slots, and spilling only affects certain warps.
Register spilling never happens because nvcc emits a compile error whenever a kernel would exceed the per-thread register budget; kernels only compile when the register file is sufficient.

explanation: CUDA 'local memory' is a misleading name: it is thread-private storage that lives in the same physical memory (GDDR/HBM) as global memory, going through the L1/L2 caches. Register spills are stores/loads of scalar values to/from this local memory. Because DRAM latency is high, heavy spilling severely hurts performance. `nvcc -Xptxas -v` reports spill stores/loads; profilers report local-memory traffic. Local memory is not shared memory (choice C), nor a special fast cache (choice B), nor a build error (choice D).

optionExplanations.A: Correct: local memory = per-thread private slice of global memory (cached).
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: not a fast on-chip cache.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: local and shared are distinct memory spaces.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: nvcc silently spills; it does not error.

assumptions: Standard CUDA memory model as documented since CUDA 1.0.
nonImplications: Does not imply all local memory accesses are slow; L1 caches many spilled accesses.
Does not imply spilling is always fatal; small amounts may be acceptable, especially for cold paths.

distractorRationales.B: Fabricates a fast on-chip local memory.
distractorRationales.D: Wrong claim that spilling errors out.
